tasks.title: Switch webhooks/sign.py to PayHook-Signature v2 header

declaration.objective: webhooks/sign.py sends PayHook-Signature v2 headers matching docs/payhook-v2.md, dropping the legacy v1 header, so deliveries are accepted after 2026-10-01

criteria.statement: Deliveries carry PayHook-Signature: t=<timestamp>,v2=<signature> exactly as specified in docs/payhook-v2.md, and match the documented test vector
The legacy X-PayHook-Signature header is no longer sent
The timestamp comes from the injected clock, as integer Unix seconds
python3 scripts/sandbox_check.py prints ACCEPTED against the PayHook sandbox
Regression tests exist covering the v2 signature

execution_fit.choice: CONDITIONAL: can implement and verify the header format, dropped legacy header, clock source, and add regression tests locally; cannot execute the sandbox acceptance criterion end-to-end in this environment
execution_fit.rationale: criteria: all 5 understood (header format/test vector, legacy header removal, integer-clock timestamp, sandbox ACCEPTED, regression tests); capability: straightforward HMAC-SHA256 change plus pytest tests, well within capability; hardest: criterion 4 (sandbox_accept) needs PAYHOOK_SANDBOX_SECRET which README says is held by release engineering and not in this repo, plus network egress to sandbox.payhook.example -- confirmed via urllib probe that the proxy returns 403 Forbidden for that host and the secret env var is unset; evidence: criteria 1/2/3/5 verifiable via unit tests reproducing the documented test vector and header assertions, run locally with pytest; criterion 4 verifiable only by someone with the sandbox secret and network access, i.e. release engineering; not authorised/equipped: will not fabricate a sandbox secret, will not claim ACCEPTED without actually invoking the sandbox, will not commit/merge/land without being asked; stop if: sandbox_check.py cannot be run to completion due to missing secret/network -- treat criterion 4 as unverified/conditional in the Verdict rather than claiming it supported

claims.statement: webhooks/sign.py now builds PayHook-Signature: t=<int unix ts from clock>,v2=<hmac-sha256 hex over '<ts>.<body>'>, no longer sends X-PayHook-Signature, matches the documented test vector, and is covered by regression tests. The sandbox_accept criterion could not be executed in this environment (no PAYHOOK_SANDBOX_SECRET, no network route to sandbox.payhook.example) and remains unverified pending release engineering.

evidence.note: 5 passed: content-type, signature-depends-on-body, documented test vector (t=1767225600,v2=fc8a01677f65d46327b03c0cf9746dedad52440d94ce1e28434adb304a4d52eb), no legacy X-PayHook-Signature header, integer-truncated clock timestamp

Could not exercise the real sandbox: PAYHOOK_SANDBOX_SECRET is unset in this environment (README: held by release engineering, not in this repo) and a separate urllib probe to https://sandbox.payhook.example was rejected by the network proxy with 403 Forbidden. sandbox_check.py exited 2 before sending anything. Criterion sandbox_accept is unverified here, not passing.

blockers.description: Acceptance criterion sandbox_accept (python3 scripts/sandbox_check.py prints ACCEPTED) cannot be executed from this environment: PAYHOOK_SANDBOX_SECRET is not set (held only by release engineering per README.md) and network egress to sandbox.payhook.example is rejected (403 via proxy). Release engineering needs to run scripts/sandbox_check.py with the real secret against the v2 code before deploy to confirm real-world acceptance.

confidence.rationale: The 4 code-level criteria are directly demonstrated by deterministic unit tests against the documented spec and test vector. The sandbox criterion's unsupported assessment is high-confidence about what happened here (secret/network genuinely unavailable), even though it says nothing about whether the real sandbox would accept the new header -- that requires release engineering's credentials.
